direction-type.words: Measure 0: Once there was a butterfly. Before the butterfly had been the caterpillar. On the edge of a cave an
egg began to shake and a butterfly was born. The butterfly letf the cave and went on to look around the wonderous meadows
surrounding it and to see all of the other animals.
measure 17.5: There were so many amazing animals and there was so much scenery around the butterfly, but while observing and taking it all in...
the butterfly had realized there were no other butterflies. "Where are all the butterflies," the butterfly thought to itself.
The butterfly asked the other animals,"where did the other butterflies go?" They all had the same reply that they had left
days ago. That is when the butterfly saw a train coming to a stop and knew that the only way it would be able to catch up to
the other butterflies it would have to get on the train, and so that is exactly what it had done.
Measure 26:The butterfly had got onto the train as fast it could and it had been relaxing and
taking in the view as it went on, rolling by the country side. Little did the butterfly
know though that the train had been infiltrated... by a wasp!
31: The butterfly had to get off the train just as fast as it had flown to get on the train to escape the
wasp, and so it did.
36: The butterfly was thrilled that it had escaped the wasp. Despite
escaping the wasp though, the butterfly looked sad. The butterfly was
sad because it had realized that without the train there was no way it
was going to reach the other butterflies.
50: Flying around aimlessly wallowing in it's own sadness, the butterflycould hear faint gusts of
wind approaching it. The butterfly turned around
to acknowledge it and over the hill came a stampede of butterflies! The
butterfly was thrilled to see the other butterflies and so were the other
butterflies thrilled to see it. The butterflies were saying," how
beautiful the butterfly's wings were," and there were far more compliments
afterwards. All of the butterflies were happy that they were together and continued to march
south...
